Integrating the January 29, 2020 FOMC statement with the Beige Book, alongside the FSR and SLOOS, shifts the tone toward near-neutral. While the FOMC characterized labor markets as strong and growth as moderate, and kept policy steady with technical operations to maintain ample reserves (not incremental easing), the Beige Book reported only modest expansion across districts, soft business fixed investment and manufacturing/exports, tight labor but moderate wage growth, and muted price pressures. Importantly, Beige Book anecdotes of tighter lending standards and softer loan demand—particularly in C&I and construction—align with SLOOS evidence of broad tightening and reduced risk tolerance. Coupled with FSR-noted vulnerabilities (elevated valuations and high corporate leverage), these factors temper the FOMC’s cautiously positive tone. Netting these inputs, the overall sentiment is slightly positive/near-neutral.
